title: Armstrong's work pace, and the band that would not back him up
summary: Randolph says the men did not support him; leaving New Orleans for Little Rock in 1934 he went door to door rousting late sidemen.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Yeah, he had a good time in life.
Boy, every night.
You were talking the last time -- you were recalling an incident in Washington, I believe, or Joe Glaser said Louis has got to make a broadcast and he's asleep, and --
Yes, uh-huh.
-- Alpha was his wife then, and she got mad because he said we're not going to wake Louis up be-
cause he has to get his rest. And you were talking about how hard he worked and he was smoking pot and that would make him work harder.

Yes, he worked pretty hard. And -- something, though, I really believe that when Louis said we're going to run this band -- say, Randolph will run the band -- run it in the ground, and said, if he does that Louis Armstrong was going in the ground with them. I think that the men didn't back us up. See, they really didn't back us up. I can recall --
You mean, they didn't play as well as they could have?
Well, no, in this way. We were supposed to leave New Orleans at a certain time, after we'd played a dance there, and go to Little Rock.
Was this '31 or '34?
No, this was in '34.
And we didn't leave until up in the day because the boys -- they was out visiting, as you know, see.
Yeah.

And so Louis told me, he says, Randy, he says, I'm going to have to take it and put it right in Mr. Glaser's hands and I'm going to have to give him the reins. And all you got -- and I didn't have nothing but just the music
to look after, see.
Yeah, it remained that way the rest of his life.
Give him the reins. See, this is the band that Mike wasn't with, this time.
I see.
He says, I'm going to give him the reins.
And Louis was trying to do it himself?
No, I had all that this time.
Oh, you had it.
I had all that.
Everything?

Everything. And so, when we got together, here's what happened. I got on the bus and stood on the steps, as the driver would drive, I'd jump out and ring the doorbell, say, okay, people, let's go, let's get ready. Well look man with the band, say, go pick up so-and-so, says, I ain't ready yet. Says, well, all right, I'd tell the driver, well, come on, let's go and get so-and-so. And we'd go there and he's not ready, so we go back and get so-and-so. And it was way up in the day before we left there.
Uh-huh.
And we had all that big jump to make and when we did get where we were going, we were late
